text:
A study of 1,622 Year 10 students across 11 regional NSW public schools tested an overseas claim that drinking water in exams boosts scores by up to 10%. Compared with the previous year, students allowed water bottles improved by 1.8 marks out of 100, and those without improved by 1.1. The 0.7-mark difference was not statistically significant.

71% of students with water said it helped them concentrate, and teachers said students seemed calmer. No problems were reported once schools required clear, label-free bottles.

**Bottom line:** Allowing water is free, low-risk and popular. Decide on comfort and wellbeing grounds, not higher marks.

**Caveats:** Schools weren't randomly assigned, and hot weather in some regions may have affected results.
